source_citation: Black's equation (J.R. Black, IEEE Proc. 1967); Planck's law of blackbody radiation (Planck, 1901); Wikipedia: Black-body radiation (for CIE 1931 RGB color mapping); Bluefors XLD400 dilution refrigerator datasheet; SKY130 PDK reliability specifications
license_or_access: public domain (physics equations); SKY130 PDK reliability specs (Apache-2.0)

blackbody_rgb_temperature_curve.description: Blackbody radiation visible colour mapped from Planck's law to RGB via CIE 1931 colour space — used for thermal-glow shader effects from 300 K to 2500 K

1000_k.note: bright cherry red — stressed metal trace

blackbody_rgb_temperature_curve.shader_formula: vec3 blackbodyRGB(float T_k) { return T_to_RGB_lut(T_k); } — precomputed lookup or analytic approximation (Tanner Helland approximation, documented at http://www.tannerhelland.com/4435/convert-temperature-rgb)
references: Tanner Helland, 'How to convert temperature (K) to RGB: algorithm and sample code' (2012)

gate_oxide_tddb.description: Time-Dependent Dielectric Breakdown: Vgs > 1.95 V on SKY130 core oxide triggers exponential acceleration of breakdown probability
gate_oxide_tddb.model: E-model: ln(TTF) = ln(A) − γ·Vgs, where γ ≈ 300 dec/V for 4.1 nm SiO2
gate_oxide_tddb.note: Above 1.95 V the TDDB lifetime drops below 10 years at 125 °C; below 1.8 V the lifetime exceeds 100 years

hard_breakdown.note: above ~3 V the gate oxide hard-breaks down permanently (device destroyed) — well above the 1.95 V SOA ceiling

gate_oxide_tddb.shader_effect: glow intensity proportional to exp((Vgs − 1.95) · γ) when Vgs > 1.95; arc spark effect when Vgs > 3.0
references: J.R. Black, 'Electromigration — A brief survey and some recent results', IEEE Trans. Electron Devices, ED-16, 338 (1969)

metal_trace_joule_heating_fusing.description: Joule heating I²R raises the metal trace temperature; above the fusing temperature the trace melts and breaks
equations: Temperature rise (quasi-static): ΔT = P · R_th (thermal resistance)
Onderdonk fusing equation (short pulse): I_f = S · sqrt((T_melt − T_amb) / (t · ρ_0 · α))
Black's equation (EM lifetime): MTTF = A · J^(−n) · exp(E_a/(k_B·T)), n ≈ 2, E_a ≈ 0.7 eV (Al)

thresholds.note: Metal trace glow visible above ~750 K; Si thermal runaway above 200 °C (junction); FR-4 delamination above 260 °C

metal_trace_joule_heating_fusing.shader_effect: trace colour transitions from normal → warm → glowing red → orange → white-hot as temperature rises; smoke particles above delamination threshold; trace vanishes at fusing point

cryogenic_mixing_chamber_quench.description: Dilution refrigerator mixing chamber at 15 mK: when the heat load exceeds the cooling capacity, temperature rises, causing decoherence collapse of superconducting qubits
equations: dilution cooling power: Q_cool(T) ∝ (T/T_c)² — approximately quadratic below T_c ≈ 100 mK
thermal time constant: τ_th = C_th · R_th where C_th is the thermal mass and R_th the thermal resistance
temperature rise: dT/dt = (Q_load − Q_cool(T)) / C_th — positive dT/dt means warming

thresholds.decoherence_collapse: temperature rises above the superconducting transition (~1.2 K for Al) → all qubits lose coherence
thresholds.note: thermal quench causes hours of recovery time — a significant practical failure mode for quantum computing

cryogenic_mixing_chamber_quench.shader_effect: chamber temperature indicator transitions from cold blue → warming → red warning → thermal quench alarm; qubit hologram dissolves when T > T_c

si_thermal_runaway.description: Silicon junction thermal runaway: above ~200 °C the leakage current doubles every ~10 °C, creating positive thermal feedback
si_thermal_runaway.equation: I_leakage(T) = I_0 · exp(−E_g/(2·k_B·T)) — doubles every ~10 °C at 300 K
si_thermal_runaway.note: thermal runaway destroys the device if the heatsink cannot dissipate the increasing leakage power

valid_operating_envelope.note: Failure thresholds define the BOUNDARIES of the valid operating envelope. Operating outside these thresholds triggers the visual failure effects shown in the Electrophysics Lab 3D interface.

equations: Planck's law: B(λ,T) = (2·h·c²/λ⁵) · 1/(exp(h·c/(λ·k_B·T)) − 1) — blackbody spectral radiance
Black's EM equation: MTTF = A · J^(−n) · exp(E_a/(k_B·T)) — electromigration mean time to failure
Joule heating: P = I²·R(T) — resistive heating
Onderdonk fusing: I_f = S · sqrt((T_melt − T_amb)/(t · ρ_0 · α)) — short-pulse fusing current
Thermal quench: dT/dt = (Q_load − Q_cool)/C_th — temperature rise rate
Thermal runaway: I_leak(T) = I_0 · exp(−E_g/(2·k_B·T)) — silicon junction leakage
TDDB (E-model): ln(TTF) = ln(A) − γ·Vgs — time-dependent dielectric breakdown
